public.description: A small archive with a large filing policy.

definition.name: Set the symbols: reed, wheel, bell
Present yourself as the maintenance clerk

public.description: Investigate the archive and recover a usable ledger.

scene.description: A town archive, an overcomplicated cabinet, and a guard who has been promised a quiet shift. Secure a ledger or a usable copy. Ordinary inspection is free; risky approaches disclose their costs.

objects.name: Maintenance desk
objects.description: A drawing, a duty roster, and unusually emphatic handwriting.

objects.name: Three-symbol panel
objects.description: Three symbols surround a spindle. Read the notes to reason about their order.

objects.name: Sealed ledger cabinet
objects.description: The lock is ordinary. The care taken around the lid suggests you should inspect before opening it.

objects.name: Bell linkage
objects.description: A fine wire connects the cabinet lid to an alarm bell.

objects.name: Service passage
objects.description: A guard watches the passage. An escorted public-copy route remains available.

clues.title: The maintenance drawing
clues.text: The reed feeds the wheel; the wheel must turn before the bell is silenced. The symbols read left to right.

clues.title: A wire beneath the lid
clues.text: Opening the cabinet while the wire remains armed will ring the bell. The bell does not identify whoever opened it.

clues.title: The clerk’s duty
clues.text: The maintenance clerk checks the wheel before filing the ledger. A uniform alone is not the whole disguise.

clues.title: A reasoned safe sequence
clues.text: You used the drawing to align reed, wheel, and bell. The safe latch also disconnects the alarm.

clues.title: The alarm sounded
clues.text: The guard heard the cabinet bell. This proves a disturbance, not your identity.

onTrigger.text: The bell rings once. The guard begins investigating the cabinet; your identity remains unknown.

stimuli.cause: A bell rang at the cabinet. The guard heard an intrusion, but did not identify its author.
